resources.string: Watchpost is not Device Owner: no policy can be applied. It is enabled through ADB, after temporarily removing the accounts: "scripts/enable-device-owner.sh" (or .ps1), see the README, section "Install and activate".

Nothing is applied without your consent: choose a profile, adjust the items, check the preview, then apply. Every action is logged (security.policy) and reversible, here or through ADB. The server cannot change any setting or policy.
The logs are set in the Collectors tab (switch of each collector).

Cuts the Samsung/Google telemetry and advertising that serve no other purpose. Google Play services, the Play Store, push notifications, payment and banking apps keep working. Re-enables the Android backup that Device Owner mode switches off.

Adds deeper de-Googling and de-Samsung-ing. May break: Samsung account, Galaxy Store, Samsung Cloud, Samsung notifications, the Google app and the Assistant, safe mode, adding certificates. The riskiest items (Google Play services, Play Store, anti-theft, payment, NFC) stay unchecked: check them one by one, knowingly.

"Uncheck everything" switches off every toggle (apps, permissions, restrictions, settings, private DNS, backup): then check only what you want to try, for example private DNS alone, then "Preview". Nothing changes on the phone before "Apply"; what is already applied and no longer checked will be restored.

Enforces DNS over TLS to your server (AdGuard Home) for the whole phone: tracker blocking and a DNS log on the server side. Before enforcing anything, Watchpost checks that the host answers DNS over TLS, otherwise the phone would lose Internet. If the host becomes unreachable for a long time, Watchpost can fall back to automatic mode (adjustable in Settings › Device Owner).
No private DNS host in the enrollment file.

Prevents changing the private DNS in Settings (disallow_config_private_dns restriction). Off by default: enforce the DNS without the lock first, check that Internet works for a few days, then lock. With the lock, if the DNS server stops answering, only Watchpost (automatic fallback, "Restore") and the ADB rescue can change the DNS.
Fallen back: the server was unreachable, DNS is in automatic mode.

"Hidden": the app disappears and its services stop. "Suspended": greyed-out icon, the app no longer opens. Packages absent from this phone are ignored; those on the deny list (Samsung lock, updates, attestation, launcher, phone, keyboard, installer, Watchpost…) are never touched.
Denies sensitive permissions to Google or Samsung apps that are kept. A permission denied by Watchpost is locked in Settings; "Restore" gives back exactly the previous state.
Never set by Watchpost: a debugging ban (it would cut ADB, the rescue door), cutting the USB signal, location sharing, factory reset, accounts, app installation, mobile network and VPN.
WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS is not granted: run "scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh" to enable these settings.
Permanent Wi-Fi scanning cannot be switched off by an app on Android 11 and later (setting stored outside Settings): Settings › Location › Location services › Wi-Fi scanning.
Becoming Device Owner switches off Android (Google) backup. The balanced profile re-enables it; the strict profile leaves it off.
Makes an installed VPN app (for example WireGuard) always-on. The "block connections without VPN" mode cuts the whole network if the VPN goes down: only enable it with a reliable VPN.
Cancels everything Watchpost applied (packages, permissions, restrictions, settings, DNS, backup, VPN) and puts back the previous state. The network and security logs stay active.

Restores everything, switches off the network and security logs, removes force-stop protection, then gives up the Device Owner role. Irreversible from the app: you will have to go through ADB again (with no accounts on the phone) to re-enable it.

If the interface no longer opens, from a computer connected with USB debugging: "scripts/rescue-revert.sh" (or .ps1) triggers "Restore everything"; "scripts/remove-device-owner.sh" (or .ps1) also removes Device Owner, like "Remove Device Owner". Only the ADB shell and the system can send this order, no other app.
Everything Watchpost applied will be undone. Continue?
Watchpost will restore everything, switch off its logs and give up the Device Owner role. To get it back, you will have to go through ADB again after removing all accounts from the phone.
Some items could not be restored (see the message). "Remove anyway" gives up the role while leaving them in place; they will have to be undone through ADB (pm unhide / pm unsuspend).
Nothing to change: the device already matches the selection.
Warning: the selection contains high-risk or critical items.
